# Every Role Has a Different Definition of a Good Shift. Now They Have a Different View.

![The Trackforce Team](https://www.trackforce.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Trackforce-Security-Software-Icon.webp)

Trackforce

June 9, 2026 · 7 min read

![Header image introducing TrackTik Job-Based Views for security operations roles](https://www.trackforce.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Every-Role-Has-a-Different-Definition-of-a-Good-Shift-Now-They-Have-a-Different-View-1-2048x1075-1.webp)

**Introducing Job-Based Views — five role-specific, live views now available to every TrackTik customer.**

Security operations don’t run on one job. They run on five, six, ten different roles, each with a completely different picture of what a good shift looks like, and what a bad one looks like before it becomes a crisis.

Most platforms treat everyone the same. Log in, navigate, click around, piece together the information you need. Then do it again tomorrow.

That works fine if you have one job. But a shift supervisor doesn’t need what a dispatcher needs. A dispatcher doesn’t need what a scheduler needs. And none of them need to spend the first hour of their day hunting for data that should already be in front of them.

That’s the problem Job-Based Views was built to solve.

## Key takeaways

- **Every role defines a good shift differently.**

A supervisor, a scheduler and a dispatcher each need a different first screen, and one generic dashboard serves none of them well.
- **The real cost is the manual assembly step.**

Checking scheduling, cross-referencing attendance and pulling a separate overtime report is pure delay, and a missed arrival becomes a client problem in under thirty minutes.
- **Five views, one operational question each.**

Shift Supervisor, Planning and Activity, Field Operations, Dispatch, and Site Activity Tracking.
- **Live means live.**

No manual refresh, no export, and no waiting for someone to compile a report before you can act.
- **Job-Based Views costs nothing extra.**

It is included for every TrackTik customer under Reporting and Analytics, with no additional license and no configuration required by the user.

## Why Role-Specific Views Matter in Security Operations

Think about how a shift supervisor actually starts their day. They need to know: who hasn’t clocked in yet, which shifts are still vacant, and who’s already in overtime territory. That’s it. Those three things determine whether the next few hours are manageable or chaotic.

Instead, they’re checking scheduling, cross-referencing attendance, pulling a separate overtime report, and making phone calls to find out what the system should already be telling them. Every manual step is a delay. In a shift-based security operation, a missed arrival becomes a coverage gap, which becomes a client problem in under thirty minutes.

The same is true for every role in the operation:

A **scheduler** needs to know where today’s coverage is breaking down, not after the shift has started, but while there’s still time to act.

A **dispatcher** needs a live task queue showing what’s unassigned, what’s aging, and what’s thirty minutes from breaching SLA.

An **operations manager** needs to know whether patrol tours are actually being completed at every site, right now, not in the end-of-week report.

A **director or account manager** needs to see incident trends rising across their book of business before a client does.

When everyone is working from the same generic view, none of these people have what they need at the moment they need it. They have data. Data isn’t the same as a decision-ready picture of their day.

## What Starting Your Day With the Right Information Actually Changes

There’s a difference between _having access to_ data and _having it ready when you open the platform_.

When the right information is surfaced for your role the moment you log in, you stop gathering context and start acting on it. You catch problems while they’re still preventable. A vacant shift surfaces two hours before it starts, not after. And the decisions you make are grounded in what’s happening right now, not what was happening when someone last ran a report.

Each view is designed around one operational question: the question that defines whether a given role is ahead of the day or behind it.

The **Shift Supervisor View** answers: _Who’s late, over OT, or missing right now, before it becomes an incident?_ It surfaces overtime exposure by employee and account, [flags vacant shifts by urgency](https://www.trackforce.com/products/tracktik/guard-management/), and shows late arrivals with elapsed time since expected clock-in.

The **Planning & Activity View** answers: _Where are my coverage gaps and shift exceptions today?_ Schedulers and planners see a real-time adherence summary, missed starts flagged the moment they occur, same-day cancellations with reason codes, and live shift status across every active site.

The **Field Operations View** answers: _Are my patrol tours actually being completed at every site?_ Operations managers see scheduled, completed, and incomplete tour counts per site — live — alongside [checkpoint compliance rates and non-compliant tours flagged for immediate action](https://www.trackforce.com/products/tracktik/security-guard-tour-system/).

The **Dispatch View** answers: _What’s unassigned right now and what’s about to breach SLA?_ [The full live task queue is visible with urgency flags](https://www.trackforce.com/products/tracktik/security-guard-dispatch/), SLA elapsed time color-coded by risk, and a task completion gauge showing overall dispatch performance for the current shift.

The **Site Activity Tracking View** answers: _Are incident volumes rising across my accounts, and what’s unresolved?_ Directors and compliance teams see [total report counts, unapproved reports flagged for immediate attention](https://www.trackforce.com/products/tracktik/security-incident-reporting/), report breakdowns by type and severity, and exposure across all sites in real time.

Every view is live. [Data refreshes continuously](https://www.trackforce.com/products/tracktik/business-intelligence/). No manual refresh, no export, no waiting for someone to compile a report.

## Available to Every TrackTik Customer — No Additional License Required

Job-Based Views is included for all TrackTik customers. There’s nothing to purchase, nothing to unlock. If your team uses TrackTik, they have access today.

Access is straightforward: Reporting and Analytics → Job-Based Views. Role permissions determine which views appear automatically for each user, so the right person sees the right view without any configuration required on their end.

The data was always there. Now it’s in the right place, for the right person, at the right time.

**Ready to see your operation in real time?** Log into TrackTik and navigate to Reporting and Analytics → Job-Based Views.

For questions, contact your Customer Success Manager or visit the [TrackTik Help Center](https://support.tracktik.com/)

## **Frequently Asked Questions**

What are Job-Based Views?

Job-Based Views are five role-specific live views available to every TrackTik customer with no additional licence required. Rather than giving every user the same generic dashboard, each role opens the platform to the information that actually determines their day.

Why does a role-specific view matter in security operations?

Security operations run on many different roles, and each has a different definition of a good shift. A shift supervisor needs to know who has not clocked in, which shifts are vacant and who is already in overtime. A dispatcher needs a live task queue showing what is unassigned, what is aging and what is close to breaching SLA. When everyone works from the same generic view, nobody has what they need at the moment they need it.

What problem does this actually solve?

It removes the manual assembly step at the start of a shift. Without role-specific views, a supervisor checks scheduling, cross-references attendance, pulls a separate overtime report and makes phone calls to learn what the system should already be showing. Every manual step is a delay, and in a shift-based operation a missed arrival becomes a coverage gap, which becomes a client problem in under thirty minutes.

Which roles are covered?

The views map to the roles that run day-to-day operations: shift supervisors, schedulers, dispatchers, operations managers, and directors or account managers who need to see incident trends rising across their book of business before a client raises them.

Do I need to buy anything to use it?

No. Job-Based Views are available to every TrackTik customer and require no additional licence.
